chirality_answer:
Chirality and R/S labels

What it means. A chiral structure cannot be superimposed on its mirror image by rotating and moving it. Such a mirror-image pair is called a pair of enantiomers.

Teach me more: why, when, where and how

Why it matters. A drawing's appearance depends on your viewing direction. Confusing a rotated view with a different configuration can lead to a wrong molecular assignment.

When to use it. Check stereochemistry when your assignment concerns chiral molecules or when importing or building stereochemical structures.

Where to find it. Inspect the selected structure in Calculations → Starting structure. Use your chemical drawing and instructor's stereochemical assignment alongside the 3D view.

How to proceed

Verify the connections and substituents, then check the specified stereochemistry in the source structure.
R/S labels follow the Cahn–Ingold–Prelog priority rules for the relevant stereogenic feature; they are not labels for the direction you rotate the image.
The signs (+)/(−) describe measured optical rotation under stated conditions. R does not generally mean (+), and S does not generally mean (−).

Scientific limits

The viewer is not an automatic stereochemical assignment or optical-rotation measurement tool.

Enantiomers have the same ordinary rotational constants and many other properties in an achiral environment; those values alone cannot distinguish them.
